# Roomr

> Roomr is the SIP and media edge for voice AI: a Go node that terminates SIP calls, mixes the
> audio of a call's participants in rooms (mix-minus, 16 kHz), and streams each call to an app over
> RTP with a per-call gRPC control stream. MIT licensed. Part of Fonoster; usable on its own.

Roomr is not an app server: no speech, prompts, recording or tenancy. A controller drives nodes
over gRPC (`roomr.v1.Roomr`); each call's app is a gRPC server (`session.v1.Session`); NATS carries
heartbeats and events, best effort.

## Docs

- [How it works](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): purpose, pieces, call flows, media path, failure model.
- [The contract](docs/CONTRACT.md): both gRPC interfaces, RTP and NATS subjects, field by field.
- [Integrate](docs/INTEGRATE.md): run a node, write an app and a controller, test it.
- [The fake](docs/FAKE.md): fonoster/roomr-fake (real nodes behind an HTTP control API) and the @fonoster/roomr npm package (client, fake client, contract suite).
- [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md): every `roomr.yaml` setting, ports, draining, codecs.
- [Performance](docs/PERFORMANCE.md): the 200-room load bar (G.711, 2 vCPU approximated with GOMAXPROCS=2) and Opus, measured.
